findings.element: The horizon's label line under the date (p.b-sub), and the first screen of a new project (states.owner-empty)
findings.problem:
The string under the date is the audience's headline everywhere the product is judged: it leads the unfurl card ("Wedding day, Saturday 3 October 2026"), it is the third line of the received phone hero, it is the whole of "Happening now" on the wedding morning, and it is the last row of the printed keepsake. In a plan built through the product it is never written by a person. Driving it: owner-empty, type "3 October 2026", Set the day, Add a moment, name it, Preview, Publish - and the card that lands in the couple's message thread reads "The day, Saturday 3 October 2026". render-b.js line ~1473 sets `F.project.primaryDate = { label: "The day", date: started }` and nothing on any of the fourteen states changes it: the horizon label is an inert

, no tabindex, no role, cursor auto. The first screen asks for the one thing it says it needs ("it is the only thing needed to start") and then silently invents the second thing, which is the one the audience actually reads first. The empty state is otherwise the best screen in the set; it asks one question well and then leaves the headline to the machine.
findings.fix: Ask for it in the same flow, once. When Set the day is accepted, the replacement b-empty block already rebuilds itself - add one more field to that rebuilt block, above the Add a moment button: label "What it is", a b-input, and the persistent hint line "For example, Wedding day." Accept any non-empty string, write it to F.project.primaryDate.label, and refuse an empty answer with the same one-sentence grammar the date field uses ("Give the day a name first. For example, Wedding day."). Never write the literal string "The day" as content. For later editing, make the horizon's label line a b-grab-style control with accessible name "Rename the day, currently Wedding day" that opens that same single field inline; it is one field, so it needs no panel.

findings.element: The last row of the measure (.b-item[data-anchor="true"]) and the editor it opens (#b-edit)
findings.problem: The renderer already knows which row is the day - it stamps data-anchor="true" on it and the behaviour gate asserts "exactly one item is the day itself" - and then hands that row the ordinary moment editor. Driving owner-flight: press Edit on the 79 row and you get "What guests see: Shown | Hidden", "Done", and "Delete this moment", with the group named "Editing Wedding day". Press Delete and the wedding day leaves the measure while the horizon 400px to the left still prints 79, still prints "Saturday 3 October 2026" and still prints "Wedding day"; the two halves of one screen now disagree about whether the plan has an end, and the only repair is an undo bar. Press Hidden and the wedding is marked "Hidden from guests" while the horizon the guests read still shows it. Type a new name in "What it is" - "Our wedding" - and the row changes and the horizon does not, because the same string lives twice in the record (fixture.js line 87 as a milestone title, line 95 as primaryDate.label). One screen, two names for one day, and the audience artifact keeps the old one. This is the library's "every fact derives from ONE accessor" class returning in the one place it costs most.
findings.fix: Derive the day's row from project.primaryDate instead of storing it as a milestone, and branch the editor on data-anchor. For the anchor row build a two-field editor - the label and the date - with the ceiling hint replaced by the standing sentence "Everything on this plan is measured from this day", and with no visibility segment, no Done-state control and no Delete. Wire the label field to project.primaryDate.label so the row title and the horizon label re-render from that one value on every keystroke, and wire the date field to project.primaryDate.date so moving the day re-scales the measure and the count together. Removing the day, if it is ever wanted, belongs on the project, not inside a control called "Delete this moment".

findings.element: The sentence under the today rule (p.b-gapNote) and the lead row's hidden unit string (.b-unitSaid on .b-item[data-lead="true"])
findings.problem: The fixed horizon keeps exactly one live line on screen at desk width and it never says what it is pointing at. At rest it reads "Nothing is planned until 1 August." - the date of the next thing, never its name. Scroll the plan pane and it becomes "22 August · 37 days away", then "19 September · 65 days away": a bare date and a bare distance sitting directly beneath a 148px "79 days", two counts stacked in one column with nothing on the surface saying they measure different things. For the stated audience - someone who has never used a tool of this kind - "22 August · 37 days away" under "79 days" is a riddle, and the row it refers to may be anywhere in a pane that scrolls independently. The same gap runs through the measure itself: the fact that one item is the next thing exists on this product only as a 6px filled dot. The lead row's spoken name is "16 days away, Menu tasting at The Orchard, Sat 1 Aug", character for character the same shape as every other row's, and the tick carries no accessible name at all. The lock's own clause - "Conditions and distances are named in words as well as drawn, so the fact exists for anyone who is not reading the picture" - is unmet for the single most useful fact on the surface.
findings.fix: Two strings. (1) In closeRun(), when the item carries data-lead="true", make its .b-unitSaid read " days away, the next thing," so the accessibility tree carries the condition; no visible label is added and the measure keeps its no-condition-labels rule. (2) In the scrolled branch of the gapNote, prefix the nearest row's title: "Final dress fitting · 22 August · 37 days away", using the same title accessor the row uses, so the pinned line always names a thing before it names a number. Leave the at-rest sentence exactly as it is; it is right.

findings.element: The editor's primary control (act("Done") in b-editActs) and the owner's folded past sentence (p.b-behindNote)
findings.problem: The editor's primary button says "Done" and sits immediately under the segment labelled "What guests see: Shown | Hidden". Three hundred pixels below it, the owner's folded past reads "2 done, the last of them 18 April." On a surface whose subject is moments that happen, a button called "Done" placed under a per-moment visibility control reads as "mark this moment done" - which is a meaning the same word carries elsewhere on the same screen - when in fact it closes the editor. The button's accessible name is the bare word, with no aria-label, so a screen-reader user gets the ambiguity undiluted. The past sentence also asserts more than the record holds: a moment behind today is reported as "done" when all the data says is that its date has passed.
findings.fix: Keep the visible word "Done" (the register is right) and give the control an accessible name that states its job: aria-label "Finished editing " + nameOf(record). Then change the owner branch of the behindBlock note from `done.length + " done, the last of them " + F.fmt.medium(last.date) + "."` to `done.length + " have happened, the last on " + F.fmt.medium(last.date) + "."` so the word "done" appears once on the screen and means one thing, and so the sentence claims only what the dates prove.

findings.element: closeRun() in render-b.js, the .b-unitSaid string for a run of more than one item (render-b.js ~line 256)
findings.problem: Two moments on one day is an ordinary thing on a wedding plan and it is reachable by driving: open "Send the invitations", press +7 until the ceiling, and it lands on 3 October beside the wedding day. The follower row correctly drops its count from the gutter - but the unit is not dropped with it, so the row's whole spoken name becomes " days away, then of 2 moments on this day, Wedding day, Sat 3 Oct". A listener gets a unit with no number in front of it, and "then of 2" is not English in any register. The lead row is better but still reads "first of 2 moments on this day" where "the first" is meant. This is the only place in fourteen states where the surface's spoken half falls below its drawn half, and it appears exactly when the plan gets busy.
findings.fix: In closeRun(), branch on i rather than appending to the unit. For i === 0: `" " + unit + ", the first of " + run.length + " moments on this day,"`. For i > 0: drop the unit entirely and use `" the same day, the " + ORDINAL[i] + " of " + run.length + " moments on it,"` with ORDINAL = ["first","second","third","fourth","fifth"] falling back to `(i + 1) + "th"`. The visible gutter stays exactly as it is.

biggestWin: The empty project and the refusals around it. "When is the day?" asks one question, states in one sentence why it is the only question, keeps the format in a line that survives typing rather than a placeholder that vanishes, and answers a wrong entry with three distinct real sentences - "Type the day first", "That is not a date", "That day has gone. Pick one still ahead" - and then, when it is answered, stops asking and becomes the count. That is a first-contact flow at the level of the named benchmarks, and it sets a bar the rest of the surface mostly meets: the folded past, the stalled load that reassures once, the printed keepsake, the unfurl card, and a horizon that genuinely makes a fortnight look like twice a week. What stands between this and 9.5 is not polish and not taste - it is one missing object. The day the whole product measures to is not modelled: it has no name a person can write (a real plan tells the couple "The day, Saturday 3 October 2026"), its name lives in two places that drift apart the moment one is edited, and the row that represents it is offered Delete, Hidden and Done like any other moment while the horizon goes on asserting it. That is a build, not a decision - roughly one field, one editor branch and one accessor, a day or two of work - and until it exists the flagship case has a hole in the exact place the audience looks first. Everything else I found is a string.
